exam: NECO Financial Accounting Part 1: Foundations, Final Accounts & Records
subject: Financial Accounting
topic: Computation of profit or loss from opening and closing balance sheets

questions.q: In a situation of incomplete records, a trader's net profit can be determined by comparing opening and closing capital. Which of the following formulas correctly calculates the net profit?
options: Closing Capital + Drawings + Additional Capital - Opening Capital
Closing Capital - Drawings + Additional Capital - Opening Capital
Closing Capital + Drawings - Additional Capital - Opening Capital
Opening Capital + Drawings - Additional Capital - Closing Capital
questions.explain:
Using a **Statement of Affairs**, the formula to ascertain profit is:
$$\text{Net Profit} = \text{Closing Capital} + \text{Drawings} - \text{Additional Capital} - \text{Opening Capital}$$
This reverses the standard Balance Sheet capital progression (where Closing Capital = Opening Capital + Net Profit + Additional Capital - Drawings).

questions.q: A trader started the year with a capital of ₦20,000. At the end of the year, total assets were ₦35,000 and total liabilities were ₦10,000. During the year, the trader withdrew ₦4,000 for personal use and introduced fresh capital of ₦5,000. What is the net profit or loss for the year?
questions.explain:
1. **Find Closing Capital:** $\text{Assets} - \text{Liabilities} = ₦35,000 - ₦10,000 = ₦25,000$.
2. **Apply Profit Formula:**
   $\text{Net Profit} = \text{Closing Capital} + \text{Drawings} - \text{Fresh Capital} - \text{Opening Capital}$
   $\text{Net Profit} = ₦25,000 + ₦4,000 - ₦5,000 - ₦20,000$
   $\text{Net Profit} = ₦29,000 - ₦25,000 = ₦4,000 \text{ profit}$.
